column4: Visit note | 2026-09-20 03:30 PM | Dr. Imran Kabir, Gastroenterology | Patient: Wasim Faruque, 41, male. Mr. Faruque presents complaining of a gnawing pain in his upper belly that often wakes him up at night. He works as a fisherman and mentions that the discomfort started after irregular meals on night shifts in Chattogram. He has no other major medical conditions and reports no jaundice, vomiting, or significant weight change. On examination, his vital signs show a pain score 7/10, along with BP 116/72 mmHg, pulse 77 bpm, and weight 52 kg. Abdominal examination reveals mild epigastric tenderness with no guarding or masses. Assessment: Peptic ulcer disease. Plan: a prescription was issued today. He was advised to avoid painkillers such as ibuprofen, stop smoking, and eat regular meals. Follow-up is scheduled in 4 weeks with a stool H. pylori test.

Visit note | 2026-09-20 04:30 PM | Dr. Imran Kabir, Gastroenterology | Patient: Orin Hossain, 72, female. Mrs. Hossain presents with an atypical presentation where she feels no pain, experiencing only early fullness and vomiting after meals instead of typical pain that wakes her at night or eases after eating. She is a retired civil servant, and her symptoms started after weeks of taking painkillers for back pain in Old Dhaka. She has a known history of Hypothyroidism. On examination, her vital signs reveal a pain score 7/10, BP 113/84 mmHg, pulse 83 bpm, and weight 68 kg. Abdominal palpation shows mild tenderness in the epigastric region. Assessment: Peptic ulcer disease. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to avoid painkillers such as ibuprofen, stop smoking, and eat regular meals. Follow-up is advised in 4 weeks with a stool H. pylori test.
